checks.name: V1 [the number a closed form would have to hit] the branch coefficient implied by kappa = 1/2 at gravitational-strength coupling is evaluated, together with the band the two independent measurements of kappa still allow
checks.measured: b = 6.684342 at kappa = 1/2; measurements allow b in [5.627, 8.592], a span of 1.53x (0.184 dex)
checks.reading: the fitted value sits comfortably inside the measured band, which is itself a fifth of a decade wide. That width is the whole problem: a band that wide will contain many tidy numbers whether or not any of them means anything

checks.name: V2 [the density of tidy numbers near the target] a systematic universe of simple closed forms is enumerated and the number of DISTINCT values falling in the decade centred on the target is counted, which is what sets whether a hit is surprising
checks.measured: 20924 distinct forms enumerated overall; 10304 of them lie in the decade 2.11 to 21.14, i.e. about one every 0.00010 dex
checks.reading: the region around the target is dense with tidy numbers. Spacing them out, there is a simple closed form roughly every few parts in ten thousand, which is far finer than anything kappa is measured to

checks.name: V3 [inside the measured band there are dozens] the enumerated forms falling inside the band the kappa measurements actually allow are counted and compared against 1, since a band containing one candidate discriminates and a band containing many does not
checks.measured: 1957 distinct simple closed forms lie inside [5.627, 8.592]
checks.reading: so hitting the band is not evidence of anything. The question 'why not this tidy expression' has dozens of equally good answers, and picking one after the fact selects nothing

checks.name: V4 [and several of them are equally consistent with the data] each candidate is converted into the kappa it implies, scored against both independent measurements, and those within two sigma of either counted
checks.measured: 6 of 6 candidates sit within two sigma of at least one measurement
checks.reading: the expression you asked about, two root eight pi over three, implies kappa = 1/sqrt(3) exactly, which is 0.62 sigma from the distance-free measurement and 1.48 from the BTFR one. It is a perfectly good candidate. So are several others, which is the point

checks.name: V5 [THE ANSWER: how much better kappa must be measured] the tolerance at which the enumerated universe contains only ONE candidate is computed from its density, converted into a required precision on kappa, and compared with the best measurement in hand
checks.measured: one candidate per 0.00010 dex = 0.022% in b; that needs kappa to 0.00011 absolute, against the current best of 0.043 -- an improvement of 385x
checks.reading: kappa would have to be measured about 385 times better than it is before a closed form hitting it carried any weight. Nothing on the observational horizon does that, and this programme's own error budget puts a floor well above it

checks.name: V6 [so the verdict, stated plainly] the question asked is answered against the enumerated density rather than against taste
checks.measured: the candidate 2 sqrt(8 pi/3) implies kappa = 0.5774, which is 1/sqrt(3) = 0.5774; 1957 enumerated rivals fit the same data; discrimination needs kappa 385x tighter
checks.reading: YES, it is numerology at the present precision -- not because the expression is ugly, but because the data cannot tell it from dozens of others. That is a statement about the measurement, not about the idea, and it would change if kappa were pinned 385 times tighter

checks.name: V7 [and there is a deeper reason it cannot be more than numerology yet] the result of L227 is applied to the question, since a coefficient that no calculation produces cannot be confirmed by a coincidence
checks.measured: L227 V5 proved no monotone interpolating function fixes b at all, and every MOND kernel is monotone by construction. So no calculation in this programme, or any sibling of it, currently outputs b
checks.reading: a closed form for b is not a prediction awaiting confirmation; it is a guess awaiting a derivation. Until some principle actually produces the number, matching it to data cannot promote it. That is the real answer, and it is structural rather than statistical

checks.name: V8 [what is recorded] the standing of kappa after this lane is stated, taking the framework's own value as given
checks.measured: kappa = 1/2 stands as the framework's fitted value; b = 6.6843 at gravitational-strength coupling is what a shape-fixing principle would have to produce; no closed form for it is evidence at current precision; and no known kernel produces it
checks.reading: the number to beat is six point six eight four. Anything that derives it from a principle would be a genuine result. Anything that merely matches it is not
